mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every injected row-pool K_(d-1,d) grid is a support-minimal squarefree unequal-cardinality equal-product relation on distinct integers at most N.
mechanisms.kill_test: Use unique prime valuations to verify shore equality, all cross-type distinctions, and the connected 0-1 subrelation kernel.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Disjoint row prime pools are unnecessary because an uncoloured single pool preserves the same row-universe counting and unique row identities.
mechanisms.kill_test: Exchange the d selected primes between two rows and test whether the same row product has multiple row identities in the counting argument.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Connectivity alone proves support minimality even if cell labels are reused on two different graph edges.
mechanisms.kill_test: Reuse a label and inspect whether its single valuation equation still forces equality of the two individual endpoint indicators.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Every transversal D of the complete grid atlas satisfies d|D_col|/m^(d-1)+|D_row|/binom(m,d)>=1 by exact marginals and a union bound.
mechanisms.kill_test: Sample ordered row injections uniformly, compute each marginal exactly, and test the strict reverse inequality by positive avoidance probability.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The products appearing at different columns of a random injected grid are mutually independent.
mechanisms.kill_test: Condition on one prime used in a row and check that it cannot reappear in another column of that row.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: One fixed dimension d proves the target subleading loss (2+o(1)) sqrt(log N log log N).
mechanisms.kill_test: Compute the fixed loss log N/d and compare it with sqrt(log N log log N).

mechanisms.decisive_claim: With d=floor(sqrt(log N/log log N)), the finite grid lower bound has logarithm log N-(2+o(1)) sqrt(log N log log N).
mechanisms.kill_test: Retain all floor errors, prime-pool losses, the factor 1/d, and the competing row-binomial term in a complete logarithmic calculation.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The inequality binom(m,d)>=m^(d-1)/d holds for every m>=d>=3.
mechanisms.kill_test: Evaluate d=m=3 and compare binom(3,3) with 3^2/3.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The prime number theorem supplies m=(1+o(1))N^(1/d)/(2 log N) primes per row pool uniformly along the optimized dimension sequence.
mechanisms.kill_test: Set x=N^(1/d), prove x tends to infinity, apply pi(x)-pi(x/2) asymptotics, divide by d-1, and simplify d log x=log N.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: Bertrand's postulate alone certifies the asymptotic pool size x/(2 log N) in the single interval (x/2,x].
mechanisms.kill_test: Separate existence of one prime from a lower bound of asymptotic order x/log x in one fixed interval.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: If a uniform adaptive valuation classifier retains its finite all-zero transcript while querying only primes below x/2, then any arbitrary global repair producing a transversal must delete at least the grid-atlas lower bound.
mechanisms.kill_test: Place every grid vertex in the zero class and apply the complete-family transversal inequality directly to the post-classification repair.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: The grid lower bound rules out every global repair of size o(N), and therefore settles the finite form of Erdos 786 negatively.
mechanisms.kill_test: Compare the proved scale with the admissible o(N) budget N/log N and recall that the original finite target is an upper-bound construction.

mechanisms.decisive_claim: An elementary-looking proof and an improved exponent automatically establish literature priority and Tier-1 publication quality.
mechanisms.kill_test: Require independent reconstruction, a primary-source literature search, and comparison with known multiplicative Sidon and cover-free grid results.
